story_type: boat aground in breaking surf at night, tethered surface swimmer wades out and walks the boater ashore
hook: His boat ran aground in the breakers as night fell.
narration: His boat had run aground in the breakers off Shackleford Banks, North Carolina.
A Coast Guard boat crew from Station Fort Macon came out, and National Park Service rangers met them.
The water was far too shallow for a rescue boat. About three feet, with waves rolling over it.
So the surface swimmer put on a harness and all his gear, and waded out on a line held by his crew.
That line matters. If a wave knocks a swimmer down in the surf, the crew on the beach can haul him back.
[short pause] He reached the boat, and the boater agreed to leave it.
outcome: The swimmer brought the boater back through the waves to the beach.
title: Aground in the surf at nightfall
description:
On June 30, 2025, a Coast Guard Station Fort Macon boat crew and National Park Service rangers rescued a mariner from the shore after his vessel ran aground near Shackleford Banks, North Carolina.
